title: Tracing the origins of CRISPR–Cas - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Reporting on a Science paper, Nature Biotechnology describes VIPR systems, small RNA-guided DNA-targeting systems found mainly in bacteriophages that may be evolutionary precursors to class 1 CRISPR-Cas. Their NN bases recognise DNA via a 'one-nucleotide skip' code and retarget without an obvious PAM requirement.

insights.claim: Yoon and colleagues describe viral interference programmable repeat (VIPR) systems, RNA-guided DNA-targeting systems that may be evolutionary precursors to class 1 CRISPR-Cas.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Understanding CRISPR origins may reveal new programmable genetic-manipulation mechanisms beyond today's editors.
insights.quote: a family of RNA-guided DNA-targeting systems that may represent evolutionary precursors to class 1 CRISPR–Cas
insights.locator: Writing in Science, Yoon and colleagues

insights.claim: Structure-based searches of the AlphaFold database found VIPR systems predominantly in bacteriophages.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: AI-predicted structure databases are being used to discover new genome-engineering tool families.
insights.quote: Using structure-based searches of the AlphaFold database, the authors identified VIPR systems predominantly in bacteriophages.

insights.claim: VIPR systems comprise a small Vipr protein bound to a VIPR RNA with tandem repeats in which conserved GGY motifs alternate with variable NN dinucleotides.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The compact two-component architecture is a potential advantage for delivery versus larger effectors.
insights.quote: Small-RNA sequencing and protein pull-down experiments showed

insights.claim: Analysis with the Evo2 genomic language model suggested the NN bases recognise DNA through a non-contiguous 'one-nucleotide skip' code, which was validated by in vitro DNA-binding assays and transcriptional repression in Escherichia coli.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A genomic language model contributed to a mechanistic discovery, an example of AI as a research tool in biotech.
insights.quote: The authors validated this ‘one-nucleotide skip’ rule using in vitro DNA-binding assays and transcriptional repression experiments in Escherichia coli.

insights.claim: Changing the NN sequences redirected VIPR to new targets on either DNA strand without an obvious requirement for the protospacer-adjacent motif used by many CRISPR-Cas systems.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Absence of an obvious PAM requirement could widen targetable sites if the system is developed as an editing tool.
insights.quote: without an obvious requirement for the protospacer-adjacent motif used by many CRISPR–Cas systems
